where: a build script that walks its environment (env::vars, a Command whose environment it changes, any child C compiler or shell): crates/blaze-cargo/src/sandbox/v2.rs, the interposers
what: Such a run was lent, and keyed by, the whole environment of the request: every variable of the user`s shell by name and value. Read from the code, not measured: any new or changed variable (another pane`s TERM, systemd`s INVOCATION_ID, a LIBCLANG_PATH added to fix two bindgen scripts) reran every script that starts a compiler. The reth miss rows `the names of every environment variable (it read them all)`, `the variable INVOCATION_ID it read` are this.
cost: not measured by this lane; the tempo rerun of 2026-11-12 (about 6,700 of 7,909 steps, 15 minutes) is what the shape predicts for the scripts, and is unconfirmed for the units behind them
cause: the rule `a walk reads all of it` was sound and the `all` was the user`s shell
whys: lending by name was built first, and a walk was given everything so that no program saw less than under cargo
nothing listed what programs a script runs take from their environment unasked
class: a key that holds an input nothing read
prevention: the walk set (blaze_usercode::confine::WALK_NAMES/WALK_PREFIXES): a walk sees that fixed list; anything else is read by name and traced; revision case a_variable_no_step_reads holds max_runs = 0
workaround: run every command of one build under one fixed environment (how-to H2)
